The first step

This build contains the player, movement, camera, and animation system. The stage has no scenery, enemies, or sound.

Animation data

Source 16 uses the right-facing row from the supplied ImageGen sheet. The frames have a common body anchor. The left view mirrors the same cycle.

Smooth 60 uses 60 computed samples in a one-second loop. Bidirectional optical flow creates the in-between frames. It can distort small details or crossing limbs. It does not create 60 new, artist-drawn poses.

Engine

Movement updates at 120 fixed steps per second. The renderer uses the browser display clock. Animation sampling is separate and supports up to 60 samples per second. The actual display rate depends on the browser and device.

Sprite textures load once. WebGL 2 draws the player. Canvas 2D is the fallback. Each clip can have its own frame count, timing, and pivot. Future 60-frame artwork can replace these samples without a new game loop.

Scope

The supplied artwork shows a run cycle, not a separate walk cycle. Stopping holds a pose. Turning mirrors the character. This build does not yet have drawn idle or turn animations.
